info.name: Play Store API - Lab 4
info.description:
Flask + MySQL REST API for the `play_store` schema (Google Play-like store).

Stack: Route -> Controller -> DTO (validation) -> Service -> DAO -> MySQL.

Resources: accounts (soft delete), devices, accounts_devices (M:N), companies, apps, categories, apps_categories (M:N), apps_versions, installations, library, reviews.

Conventions: GET list, GET by id, POST (201), PUT (full update), PATCH (partial), DELETE (204). JSON bodies use Content-Type: application/json. Unknown or missing fields return 400; missing rows return 404.

Soft deletion:
- DELETE /accounts/:id sets `deleted_at` (soft delete); the account is excluded from GET /accounts and returns 404 afterwards. All apps owned by that developer's company are unpublished (suspended apps keep their moderation state).
- DELETE /apps/:id hard-deletes (204) when the app has no versions, library entries, or reviews; otherwise it soft-deletes by setting status='unpublished' and returns 200 with the app JSON. Repeating is idempotent and never downgrades a suspended app.

Tests: the DELETE requests for accounts and apps contain Postman test scripts (and saved example responses) that verify these semantics.

item.name: accounts
item.description: Account CRUD. Accounts are soft-deleted: DELETE sets deleted_at, the row is kept, soft-deleted accounts vanish from GET /accounts and return 404 on GET /accounts/:id. Deleting a developer account also unpublishes every app owned by that developer's company (apps already 'suspended' keep their moderation state). Responses never include the password hash.

request.description: List all active accounts.
Fetch one account by id (404 if missing or soft-deleted).
Create an account. Required: email, password (min 8 chars), name.
Full update. All writable fields required: email, password, name.
Partial update. At least one of: email, password, name.

Soft-delete a developer account. The account row is kept and `deleted_at` is set; the account then returns 404 and is excluded from GET /accounts. Every app owned by the developer's company is unpublished (status='unpublished'); apps already 'suspended' keep that state and are never downgraded. Existing versions, library entries, and reviews stay intact. Returns 204 No Content.

Tests: asserts 204, verifies GET /accounts/:id returns 404, and verifies the developer's apps are no longer 'published'.

item.name: companies
item.description: Company CRUD. developer_id references accounts.id (1:1 with an account).

request.description: List all companies.
Fetch one company by id.
Create a company. Required: company_name, developer_id. contact_email is optional and may be null.
Full update. Required: company_name, contact_email, developer_id.
Partial update. At least one of: company_name, contact_email, developer_id.
Delete a company. Returns 204 No Content.
List all categories.
Fetch one category by id.
Create a category. Required: name (max 45 chars, unique).
Full update. Required: name.
Partial update. Required: name.
Delete a category. Returns 204 No Content.

item.name: apps
item.description: App CRUD. status is one of published | unpublished | suspended (defaults to published). DELETE soft-deletes apps that still have versions/library entries/reviews (status='unpublished', 200) and hard-deletes apps without dependents (204).

request.description: List all apps.
Fetch one app by id.
Create an app. Required: title, package_name, company_id. Optional: caption, status.
Full update. Required: title, package_name, caption, company_id, status.
Partial update. At least one of: title, package_name, caption, company_id, status.

Delete an app.

- **No versions, library entries, or reviews** -> hard delete (row removed), **204 No Content**.
- **Has dependents** -> soft delete: `status` becomes `unpublished`, the row is kept, **200 OK** with the updated app JSON (same shape as GET /apps/:id).
- Repeated DELETE while unpublished/suspended is idempotent: **200** with the current JSON. A `suspended` app is never downgraded to `unpublished`.
- Existing versions, library entries, and reviews stay intact and readable after a soft delete.

Tests: accepts 200 or 204, asserts the app is not published afterwards (GET returns 404 or status unpublished/suspended).

item.name: apps_versions
item.description: App version CRUD. (app_id, version) is unique; size_bytes is a BIGINT UNSIGNED.

request.description: List all app versions.
Fetch one app version by id.
Create a version. Required: app_id, version, size_bytes.
Full update. Required: app_id, version, size_bytes.
Partial update. At least one of: app_id, version, size_bytes.
Delete an app version. Returns 204 No Content.
List all installations.
Fetch one installation by id.
Create an installation. Required: device_id, app_version_id.
Full update. Required: device_id, app_version_id.
Partial update. At least one of: device_id, app_version_id.
Delete an installation. Returns 204 No Content.

item.name: library
item.description: Library entry CRUD. (account_id, app_id) is unique.

request.description: List all library entries.
Fetch one library entry by id.
Create a library entry. Required: account_id, app_id. Optional: last_opened_at (ISO 8601), data_ref.
Full update. Required: account_id, app_id, last_opened_at, data_ref.
Partial update. At least one of: account_id, app_id, last_opened_at, data_ref.
Delete a library entry. Returns 204 No Content.

item.name: reviews
item.description: Review CRUD. Review must reference an existing (account_id, app_id) library entry. rating is 0.0-5.0 with at most one decimal digit.

request.description: List all reviews.
Fetch one review by id.
Create a review. Required: account_id, app_id, rating. Optional: comment. Requires an existing library entry for the same (account_id, app_id) - run 'library > POST create' first.
Full update. Required: rating, comment.
Partial update. At least one of: rating, comment.
Delete a review. Returns 204 No Content.
